intro_html: Bangers and mash is British pub food at its most honest: sausages, buttery mashed potatoes, peas, and an onion gravy poured over the whole thing. The sausages got the nickname because wartime versions had so much water in them they burst in the pan. Ours do not, and this plate carries 39 grams of protein for about $3.06 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $3.06 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a full pub plate with gravy. Potatoes and onions are the two cheapest staples on the board, which is exactly why this dish survived a century of hard times.
shop_smart: Sausages are the entire budget here. Everything else on the list barely moves the needle. Buy them on sale, freeze them, and the cost of this recipe drops hard.
Buy potatoes in the big bag. This uses a serious amount of them for the mash, and bagged potatoes cost roughly half what loose ones do per pound.
Frozen peas are the right peas. They are picked and frozen at peak, they cost less than fresh, and they need nothing but a minute of heat.
The gravy is butter, flour, onions and broth. A splash of soy sauce is the trick that gives it the dark color and savory depth people assume comes from a packet.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and chunk the potatoes and get them going in salted water. Slice the onions thin and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and brown the sausages slowly on all sides. Low and slow keeps the casings from splitting.
Move the sausages to a plate and start the gravy in the same pan, melting most of the butter and cooking the sliced onions until they go deep golden and sweet.
Add the garlic, then sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute before streaming in the chicken broth while whisking.
Add the soy sauce and simmer the gravy until it thickens and coats a spoon, then season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the potatoes, mash them with the remaining butter, salt and pepper, and keep them loose enough to portion easily.
Warm the peas through, slice the sausages into thick coins, and combine everything with the gravy in your big pot.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, mash first and then sausage and gravy over it. Every bowl lands near 879 calories and 39 grams of protein.

head.description: British bangers and mash with buttery mashed potatoes, peas and a rich onion gravy. 14 servings, 879 calories, 39g protein, about $3.06 each (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: bangers and mash, onion gravy, sausage and mashed potatoes, british comfort food, budget meal prep
steps: Boil the peeled and chunked potatoes in salted water.
Brown the sausages slowly in vegetable oil, then set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in butter until deep golden, add the garlic, then stir in the flour.
Stream in the chicken broth and soy sauce and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Mash the potatoes with butter, warm the peas, slice the sausages, and combine with the gravy.
